confirm the id-form trap is real: does list_reports_v2 (the v2 listing an agent would naturally reach for) ever expose the integer id, or only SC-NNN?

The gap is large and non-obvious (95008 vs 12541), not an off-by-one a caller might rationalize away.

notes:
PREPROD (tests/live/runs/tm/get_report_detail.json): DRIFT — data.mail_to declared-required-but-absent was not the headline finding there (preprod's file centered on report_data's undeclared drilldown-replacement shape and the is_dynamic/filters prose gap); this prod run additionally nails down the data.mail_to / 7-undeclared-fields pattern and ties it explicitly to the create_report/update_report shared-serializer finding (tests/live/findings/create_report_v2.md and runs/tm/{create_report,update_report}.json), which prod now confirms extends to this read capability. PROD RESULT: DRIFT reproduces.

1) ID-FORM TRAP: REAL and confirmed sharply on real prod data. list_reports_v2 exposes only 'SC-12541'; stripping the prefix gives 12541, but the true integer id (from list_schedules) is 95008 — a difference of tens of thousands, because SC-NNN is a per-group sequence number unrelated to the row id. A caller who strips the prefix gets a 404 or (worse) a different report entirely if some other report happens to have id 12541 in a different group. Only list_schedules exposes id+identifier together, exactly as preprod's guidance says.

2) BARE vs SECTIONS: confirmed on real, non-trivial prod data. Bare call (report_id 95008, no query): report_data.test_run_data populated ({active:17,closed:0,test_cases:139,test_results:141}); issues_data/test_run_status/test_cases_status/issues_by_status/issues_by_priority/time_tracking/estimated_vs_actual all null. Same call with sections=test_run_data,issues_data,test_run_status,test_cases_status,issues_by_status,issues_by_priority: every named section switched from null to a populated value — issues_data {total:0,...}, test_run_status {New:2,In_Progress:0,Under_Review:0,Rejected:0,Done:153,Closed:0}, test_cases_status a real 56-entry array of this group's configured result statuses (Passed:100, Failed:37, Retest:1, Conditionally Passed:1, rest 0), issues_by_status/issues_by_priority both moved from null to real (empty) arrays []. time_tracking/estimated_vs_actual, NOT named in sections, stayed null. This is exactly the documented 'null means NOT COMPUTED' behavior, verified with real non-zero counts rather than an empty project.

3) report_data_only TRAP: verified true with the literal string 'false'. report_data_only="false" on report_id 95008 returned only the bare report_data object ({test_run_data, issues_data:null, ...}) — no data, no report_filters, no project, no envelope at all. This is truthy-string coercion exactly as documented; it is confirmed real, not merely asserted by the docs.

4) is_print=true: CONFIRMED to actually force all sections, on BOTH report types, and is NOT a silent no-op (unlike update_filter's inert entity / minify). Test Run Summary (95008): is_print=true populated test_run_data, issues_data, test_run_status, test_cases_status (56-entry array), user_result_stats, issues_by_status, issues_by_priority, AND time_tracking ({total_elapsed_seconds:0, cases_with_elapsed:0, cases_in_scope:2}) and estimated_vs_actual ([]) plus the undeclared time_tracking_enabled:false — the last two sections never appear even when sections= names everything except them, so is_print visibly does more than a hand-picked sections list. Test Plan Summary (94997): compared bare (report_data: {test_plans_execution_trend_list: []} — a SINGLE key, everything else absent) against is_print=true (report_data: 12 keys — test_plans_near_completion, overdue_test_plans, test_run_data, test_plans_progress, test_plans_execution_trend_list, test_plans_execution_trend_graph, test_result_user_stats, test_run_requirements, test_result_defects, defects_by_status, defects_by_priority, test_run_status). The values are mostly 0/[] because this Test Plan Summary genuinely has no qualifying test-plan activity in its last_one_month window (test_plans_progress.total_count:0), but the KEY SET size (1 -> 12) is the proof is_print did real work, independent of whether the underlying counts happen to be zero — distinguishing 'is_print is a no-op' from 'is_print computed real zeros' cleanly.

5) Defects Summary / Defects Detailed Report: CONFIRMED ABSENT from this project (list_schedules q[query]=Defects -> total_report_count:0). Per the capability's own guidance these types always read back report_data:null with no data branch at all; that specific null-forever behavior could not be exercised here because no such report exists in this project to read — recorded as an honest absence, not conflated with a wrong section name (which would 400, not silently return null).

6) tr_drilldown 401 — NEW PROD-ONLY FINDING, not present in the preprod run: sections=tr_drilldown&widget_type=active_runs (and widget_type=tcs_by_status) on report 95008, and again on an unrelated second Test Run Summary report (94963, SC-12533), both consistently returned HTTP 401 {"success":false} — reproduced 4 times across 2 reports and 2 widget_types, with no other call in this session (bare, sections, is_print, or a DIFFERENT drilldown type) ever 401ing. tc_activity_drilldown on a Test Case Activity report (94964) in the SAME project succeeded normally (200, real paginated rows, total:7/rows.length:7/info:{page:1,page_size:7} all consistent). So drilldowns are not uniformly broken — this is specific to tr_drilldown on Test Run Summary reports in this environment/session. Preprod's get_report_detail run got a clean 200 with 30 rows for the identical sections=tr_drilldown&widget_type=active_runs combination — so this is a genuine PREPROD-VS-PROD BEHAVIORAL DIFFERENCE, not a repeat of a known preprod defect. Cause not diagnosed (could be a permission scope this session/user lacks specifically for tr_drilldown, or a real regression) — reported as an observed, reproducible fact per the shallowest-missing-path rule, without further downstream guessing. COUNT-VS-ROWS / PAGINATION for tr_drilldown could NOT be exercised on prod as a result (BLOCKED for that specific sub-check); the tc_activity_drilldown call that did succeed showed count(total)=7 exactly equal to rows.length=7, consistent, and correctly not something to sum into any other total.

7) SHARED-SERIALIZER CHECK (the 'ALSO CHECK' item): data.mail_to is declared required in get_report_detail's own schema and is absent from data in every single call made here, on two different report types — this is the identical gap create_report/update_report showed on preprod (data.mail_to required-but-absent). The SAME 7 undeclared fields (updated_at, project_ids, included_projects, is_dynamic, grain, slack_notification, slack_notification_supported) also appear on data here, matching create_report/update_report's undeclared_returned list exactly. This is strong evidence the shared-serializer problem is not confined to the two write capabilities — it extends to this read capability too, since get_report_detail almost certainly re-serializes the same underlying report record through the same code path. Notably, the SIBLING v2 listing (list_reports_v2) DOES include mail_to on every row ({"users":[],"external_mails":[]}) — so the field exists and is queryable, it is simply dropped by whatever serializer get_report_detail (and create_report/update_report) share, which v2's serializer does not share.

COUNT-VS-ROWS elsewhere: list_schedules info.count (1197) matches total_report_count (1197) exactly, both matching the true number of rows across all pages — no drift there. Drilldown rows (tc_activity_drilldown) were correctly treated as a page of items, not summed.

no write, no email: only read capabilities and list_* discovery reads were invoked. send_report_email_now_v1 was never called and no parameter on any of these calls was touched that could plausibly trigger a send (mail_to, frequency, frequency_details were never set — they are absent/null throughout, and this capability has no send-adjacent parameter at all).
